qualification.reason: The document is a Request for Proposals (RFP) issued by the City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County for a planning project, including submission deadlines, scope of work, minimum qualifications, and evaluation criteria, clearly indicating a procurement solicitation.

quotes.quote: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS
Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST

The City/County Association of Governments of San Mateo County (C/CAG), a Joint Powers Agency composed of the County of San Mateo and all twenty cities located within San Mateo County, invites qualified consultants to submit proposals for San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project
Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026

findings.title: Litigation Disclosure
findings.fact: Proposers must indicate if they are or were involved in litigation in connection with prior projects and describe the nature and result.

quotes.quote: Indicate if the proposing consultant is or was involved with any litigation in connection with prior projects. If yes, briefly describe the nature of the litigation and the result.

findings.title: References Requirement
findings.fact: Proposers must provide three to five references for work completed within five years of the RFP issuance, with accessible contact information.

quotes.quote: Provide three to five references (no more than five including references for subcontractors) and their contact information. References should be for work completed within five years of the date of the issuance of this RFP, and the contact person must be currently accessible via the contact information provided to be considered.

findings.title: Work Samples Requirement
findings.fact: Proposers must provide at least one sample of a written technical report or memo and one sample of material developed for a similar study effort, prepared by key team members.

quotes.quote: Provide at least one sample of a written technical report or memo and one sample of material developed for a similar study effort. The samples must have been prepared by key members of the proposer’s team and should identify the authors.

findings.title: Firm Offer Period
findings.fact: Proposal must indicate it is a firm offer to enter into a contract for a period of 120 days from the due date for proposals.

quotes.quote: Indicate that the proposal is a firm offer to enter into a contract to perform work related to this RFP for a period of 120 days from the due date for proposals.

findings.title: Acknowledgment of RFP and Addenda
findings.fact: Proposal must acknowledge receipt of the RFP and any addenda.

quotes.quote: Acknowledge the receipt of this RFP and any addendum to the RFP.

findings.title: Conflict of Interest Statement in Cover Letter
findings.fact: Cover letter must indicate any conflicts of interest and describe mitigation plans.

quotes.quote: Indicate whether there are any conflicts of interest, actual or apparent, that would limit the proposer’s ability to provide the requested services and describe the plan for mitigating such conflicts.

findings.title: References Requirement
findings.fact: Proposal must provide at least three references from agencies consulted in the past three years.

quotes.quote: Provide as reference the names of at least three agencies you currently or have previously consulted for in the past three years.

findings.title: Right to Reject and Negotiate
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to reject any and all proposals, waive minor irregularities, and negotiate with any or all proposers.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to reject any and all proposals, waive minor irregularities, request additional information, or revisions to offers, negotiate with any or all proposers, and waive any requirements of this RFP when it determines that waiving a requirement is in the best interest of C/CAG.

findings.title: Failure to Enter Contract
findings.fact: If the selected proposer fails to enter into a contract in a timely manner, C/CAG may reject the proposal and contract with the next highest scoring proposer.

quotes.quote: If the selected proposer fails to enter into a contract with C/CAG in a timely manner as determined by C/CAG, C/CAG reserves the right to reject the proposal and enter into a contract with the next highest scoring proposer.

findings.title: Rating Scale
findings.fact: Proposals are scored on a 0-5 rating scale with defined descriptors for each score.

findings.title: Oral Interviews
findings.fact: The selection process may include oral interviews, and if held, they are evaluated based on presentation and Q&A criteria.

quotes.quote: The selection process may include oral interviews. If oral interviews are necessary, the consultant will be notified of the time and place of oral interviews and whether any additional information may be required to be submitted. The evaluation criteria for the oral interviews, should they occur, are included below.

8. Presentation by Team (10 points) (if oral interviews are necessary) 
• Team presentation conveying project understanding, communication skills, innovative ideas, critical issues and solutions. 

9. Q&A Response to Panel Questions (10 points) (if oral interviews are necessary) 
• Proposer provides responses to various interview panel questions.

findings.title: Selection Disputes
findings.fact: Proposers may protest RFP provisions or selection decisions within specified deadlines.

quotes.quote:
A proposer may object to a provision of the RFP on the grounds that it is arbitrary, biased, or unduly restrictive, or to the selection of a particular proposer on the grounds that C/CAG procedures, the provisions of the RFP or applicable provisions of federal, state, or local law have been violated or inaccurately or inappropriately applied by submitting a written protest to the C/CAG Project Manager in accordance with the following deadlines: 
1. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions. 
2. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive. 
3. No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: Best and Final Offer Stage
findings.fact: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

findings.title: Protest Deadlines
findings.fact: Proposers may object to RFP provisions or selection decisions by submitting a written protest to the C/CAG Project Manager within specified deadlines.

quotes.quote: A proposer may object to a provision of the RFP on the grounds that it is arbitrary, biased, or unduly restrictive, or to the selection of a particular proposer on the grounds that C/CAG procedures, the provisions of the RFP or applicable provisions of federal, state, or local law have been violated or inaccurately or inappropriately applied by submitting a written protest to the C/CAG Project Manager in accordance with the following deadlines:

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Three Projects in Past Ten Years
findings.fact: Proposer must demonstrate that the prime consultant and/or subconsultant have successfully completed at least three projects in the past ten years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report, Vision Zero Action Plan, or supplemental/implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. If the bidder cannot demonstrate three relevant projects, their proposal will be deemed non-responsive and rejected. This could disqualify the bidder from consideration.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the firm's project portfolio to confirm at least three qualifying projects within the last ten years. If necessary, identify subconsultants with relevant experience to meet this requirement. Prepare detailed project descriptions and references to include in the proposal.

quotes.quote: Proposer must demonstrate to C/CAG’s satisfaction that the prime consultant and/or one or more subconsultant proposed this project have successfully completed at least three (3) projects in the past ten (10) years related to Local Roadway Safety Plan, Systemic Safety Analysis Report (SSAR), Vision Zero Action Plan and/or supplemental or implementation planning for the Safe Streets for All Grant Program.

findings.title: Minimum Qualifications: Federal Grant Experience
findings.fact: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements.
findings.business_implication: This is a mandatory qualification. Lack of demonstrated experience with federal grants could result in disqualification. The bidder must prove they can handle the compliance and management requirements of a federally funded project.
findings.action_recommendation: Highlight past federal grant projects in the proposal, emphasizing the scale and compliance aspects. Provide examples of successful management and compliance with federal, state, and local regulations. If the firm lacks this experience, consider partnering with a subconsultant who has it.

quotes.quote: Proposers must demonstrate experience managing and implementing large-scale federal grant funded projects and successfully ensuring compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local requirements for such projects.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Requirements
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, via email with specific subject line. Late proposals may be considered nonresponsive.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline could result in the proposal being rejected as nonresponsive. The bidder must ensure timely submission to be considered.
findings.action_recommendation: Mark the deadline on calendars and set internal reminders. Prepare the proposal well in advance and submit it early to avoid last-minute issues. Ensure the email subject line is exactly as specified and sent to the correct address.

quotes.quote: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP. Proposals should be emailed with the subject line “RFP – San Mateo Countywide Safe Streets for All Supplemental Planning Project” to: Eva Gaye (egaye@smcgov.org).
Proposals received after the time and date specified above may be considered nonresponsive.

findings.title: Proposal Format and Page Limit
findings.fact: Proposals must be submitted as one electronic PDF, with pages 8.5x11 or 11x17, sequentially numbered, with table of contents, and no more than 20 pages excluding specified sections.
findings.business_implication: Failure to comply with formatting and page limits may lead to rejection or negative evaluation. The bidder must ensure the proposal meets all formatting requirements to be considered.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully format the proposal according to the specifications. Use the allowed page size, number pages sequentially, include a table of contents, and keep the main body within 20 pages (excluding cover letter, title page, TOC, resumes, relevant experience, and references). Review the final PDF to ensure compliance.

quotes.quote: Consultants must submit one (1) electronic copy of the proposal in pdf format. Each page shall be 8.5” x 11” or 11” x 17”. Each page shall be sequentially numbered, and a table of contents shall be provided. Each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references.

findings.title: Signature Requirement
findings.fact: Unsigned proposals or proposals signed by an individual not authorized to bind the prospective consultant will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.
findings.business_implication: This is a strict requirement. If the proposal is not signed by an authorized individual, it will be rejected. The bidder must ensure proper authorization and signature.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal is signed by an individual with authority to bind the company. Verify that the signatory's title and authority are clear. Double-check the signature page before submission.

quotes.quote: Unsigned proposals or proposals signed by an individual not authorized to bind the prospective consultant will be considered nonresponsive and rejected.

findings.title: Conflict of Interest Disclosure
findings.fact: Proposers must include a Conflict of Interest Statement disclosing any financial, business, or other relationship with C/CAG that may impact the outcome of the contract, and list current clients with potential financial interest.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must proactively identify and disclose any relationships with C/CAG or clients that could be perceived as a conflict, as failure to do so could lead to disqualification or contract termination.
findings.action_recommendation: Review all current and past relationships with C/CAG and its board members, and prepare a comprehensive Conflict of Interest Statement. If any potential conflicts exist, outline mitigation strategies to avoid or eliminate them.

quotes.quote: Include a Conflict of Interest Statement disclosing any financial, business or other relationship with C/CAG that may have an impact upon the outcome of the contract. List current clients who may have a financial interest in the outcome of this contract.

findings.title: Project Examples Requirement
findings.fact: Proposers must demonstrate successful completion of comparable projects, including a detailed description of at least three projects within the past five years with specified information.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must provide evidence of relevant past performance to prove capability, which is a key evaluation criterion. Lack of comparable projects could weaken the proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Identify at least three projects completed in the last five years that are similar in scope and complexity. For each, compile all required details (contracting agency, contact, amount, funding source, dates, outcomes) and highlight how they demonstrate the team's ability to deliver this project.

quotes.quote: Demonstrate successful completion of comparable projects. These projects must illustrate the quality, type, and past performance of the project team. Include a detailed description of a minimum of three projects within the past five years, with the following information:

findings.title: Key Personnel Commitment
findings.fact: Key personnel, especially the project manager, must have significant demonstrated experience and ideally be committed to stay with the project for its duration. Changes require prior written approval.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that the proposed key personnel are experienced and likely to remain on the project, as any changes could be considered a material breach and require C/CAG approval.
findings.action_recommendation: Select a project manager and key staff with strong relevant experience and a commitment to the project timeline. Include their resumes and references, and ensure they are aware of the no-change policy. If any changes are anticipated, discuss with C/CAG early.

quotes.quote: Key members, especially the project manager, shall have significant demonstrated experience with this type of project, and ideally should be committed to stay with the project for its duration. Any change in key personnel on the project team is subject to prior written approval of C/CAG.

findings.title: Federal Compliance Requirement
findings.fact: Any contract resulting from this RFP will be funded with federal funds and subject to all applicable federal laws and regulations, including those in the Grant Agreement.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be prepared to comply with extensive federal requirements, which may include additional reporting, audit, and compliance obligations. Non-compliance could result in penalties or loss of funding.
findings.action_recommendation: Thoroughly review the Grant Agreement (Appendix B) and Exhibit A to understand all federal requirements. Ensure the bidder has experience with federally funded projects and can demonstrate capability to meet these obligations. Consider designating a compliance officer.

quotes.quote: Any contract entered into as a result of this RFP will be funded, in whole or in part, with federal funds administered by the FHWA. Accordingly, federal requirements apply to this procurement, any resulting agreement, and the services to be provided.

Financial assistance for the services described in this RFP will be fully or partially provided using funds from the FHWA. Any contract and subcontract to provide the services described in this RFP will be subject to the Grant Agreement in Appendix B between C/CAG and FHWA and will be subject to all applicable federal laws and regulations as set forth in Exhibit A to the Grant Agreement.

findings.title: Mandatory Federal Certifications and Forms
findings.fact: Proposals must contain three federal certifications/forms: Certification Regarding Lobbying, Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.
findings.business_implication: Failure to include these mandatory forms will render the proposal nonresponsive and lead to rejection. The bidder must ensure all forms are correctly completed and signed.
findings.action_recommendation: Obtain the latest versions of the three required forms from the FHWA website, complete them accurately, and include them in the proposal. Double-check that all signatures are in place and that the forms are not counted against the page limit.

quotes.quote: Proposals must contain the following federal certifications or forms: (1) Certification Regarding Lobbying, (2) Certification Regarding Debarment, Suspension, Ineligibility, and Voluntary Exclusion—Lower Tier Covered Transactions, and (3) Disclosure of Lobbying Activities (SF-LLL) form.

findings.title: Insurance Acknowledgement Requirement
findings.fact: Proposer must submit a signed acknowledgement agreeing to provide required certificates of insurance within ten days of notice of selection.
findings.business_implication: Failure to submit the signed acknowledgement will render the proposal non-responsive and lead to disqualification. Additionally, the successful proposer must be prepared to provide insurance certificates within a tight 10-day window after selection, which requires advance coordination with insurance providers.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the signed acknowledgement is included in the proposal package. Prepare in advance by contacting insurance brokers to expedite the issuance of certificates of insurance, and have a clear internal process to meet the 10-day deadline if selected.

quotes.quote: Submit a signed acknowledgement, for proposer only, that the proposer agrees to provide the required certificates of insurance providing verification of the minimum insurance requirements listed in Appendix D, Sample Agreement Template (see Section 11), within ten days of C/CAG’s notice to firm that it is the successful Proposer.

findings.title: Non-Responsive Submittals Disqualified
findings.fact: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff's discretion.
findings.business_implication: Any missing required document or form can lead to immediate disqualification without the opportunity to cure. This places a premium on meticulous compliance with all RFP instructions.
findings.action_recommendation: Create a detailed compliance checklist based on the RFP requirements and conduct a thorough internal review before submission. Have a second person independently verify completeness to minimize the risk of oversight.

quotes.quote: An incomplete submittal will be deemed non-responsive and disqualified at C/CAG staff’s discretion.

findings.title: Proposal Submission Deadline
findings.fact: Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12:00 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Missing the deadline will result in the proposal being considered non-responsive and rejected. Late submissions are not accepted, and C/CAG is not responsible for delays.
findings.action_recommendation: Submit the proposal well in advance of the deadline to avoid last-minute technical issues. Use reliable electronic submission methods and confirm receipt with C/CAG. Plan internal milestones to finalize the proposal at least 2-3 days before the due date.

quotes.quote: Proposals are due: January 23, 2026, 12:00PM PST
Proposals must be received by C/CAG no later than 12 PM PST on Friday, January 23, 2026, in accordance with the instructions contained in the RFP.
12:00 PM PST, Friday, January 23, 2026 RFP Proposals Due

findings.title: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications
findings.fact: The deadline for requests for clarifications is January 9, 2026.
findings.business_implication: Any questions or requests for clarification must be submitted by this date. Missing this deadline means the proposer will not receive answers to their questions, potentially leading to misunderstandings or non-compliance.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly and submit all clarification requests well before January 9, 2026. Monitor C/CAG's website for addenda and incorporate any clarifications into the proposal.

quotes.quote: Deadline for Requests for Clarifications: January 9, 2026
Friday, January 9, 2026 Question and Answer Deadline

findings.title: Modified Proposals Deadline
findings.fact: Modified proposals must be received prior to January 23, 2026.
findings.business_implication: If the proposer needs to withdraw or modify their proposal, the modified version must be received before the submission deadline. This allows for corrections but only if done in time.
findings.action_recommendation: If any changes are needed after initial submission, ensure the modified proposal is submitted well before January 23, 2026. Keep track of the deadline and have a process in place for submitting modifications.

quotes.quote: To be considered for the project, however, a modified proposal must be received prior to January 23, 2026.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for RFP Provisions
findings.fact: Objections to RFP provisions must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must identify any objectionable RFP provisions early in the proposal preparation process, as the deadline is before the proposal submission date.
findings.action_recommendation: Review the RFP thoroughly immediately upon receipt and submit any objections by the specified deadline, ensuring compliance with the protest procedure.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day prior to the date Responses to RFP are due, for objections to RFP provisions.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for Non-Responsive Determination
findings.fact: Protests regarding non-responsive determination must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is deemed non-responsive, there is a very short window to challenge the determination, which could impact the ability to compete for the contract.
findings.action_recommendation: Be prepared to act quickly if notified of non-responsiveness; have a process in place to draft and submit a protest within the three-business-day deadline.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it did not meet the minimum qualifications or was found to be non-responsive.

findings.title: Protest Deadline for Award Decision
findings.fact: Protests regarding award decision must be submitted no later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later.
findings.business_implication: If the bidder is not selected, there is a limited time to protest the award decision, which may affect the ability to overturn the decision.
findings.action_recommendation: Monitor notifications closely and be ready to file a protest within three business days if the award is unfavorable; consider seeking legal advice promptly.

quotes.quote: No later than 5:00 p.m. on the third business day after the date on which the proposer is notified that it was not selected, or, if applicable, the date the Committee recommends award, whichever is later, for objections to the recommended award.

findings.title: Most Advantageous Proposal
findings.fact: The contract will be awarded to the responsible proposer whose proposal is most advantageous to C/CAG, with price and other factors considered.
findings.business_implication: The award is not solely based on price; other factors such as qualifications, approach, and references are considered, so the bidder must present a compelling overall proposal.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a proposal that clearly demonstrates value beyond price, highlighting strengths in all evaluation criteria to be the most advantageous.

quotes.quote: Any contract resulting from this RFP will be awarded to the responsible proposer whose proposal is most advantageous to C/CAG, with price and other factors considered.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria Weights
findings.fact: The evaluation criteria include written criteria (Organization, Staff/Firm Qualifications, Understanding of Scope, Proposed Approach, Cost Effectiveness, References, Conflict of Interest) and interview criteria (Presentation, Q&A), with weights totaling 100.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must allocate effort according to the weights: Staff/Firm Qualifications and Understanding of Scope are the most heavily weighted written criteria (20 each), while the interview contributes 20% to the total score.
findings.action_recommendation: Focus proposal development on the highest-weighted criteria, ensuring strong team qualifications and deep understanding of the scope; prepare thoroughly for the interview as it can significantly impact the final score.

quotes.quote:
The evaluation criteria summary and their respective weights are as follows: 
No. Written Evaluation Criteria Weight 
1 Organization of Proposal 5 
2 Staff and Firm Qualifications 20 
3 Understanding of Project Scope of Work 20 
4 Proposed Project Approach 15

7 Conflict of Interest Statement Pass/Fail 
 Subtotal: 80

 Subtotal: 20 
 Total: 100

findings.title: Recommendation for Contract Award
findings.fact: C/CAG may award based on initial proposals without interviews, and reserves the right to negotiate or include a best and final offer stage.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must submit its most competitive proposal upfront, as there may be no opportunity for interviews or revisions. The evaluation will be based solely on the initial submission, so any weaknesses could be decisive.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure the proposal is comprehensive, technically strong, and priced competitively from the start. Prepare for the possibility of negotiations or a best and final offer (BAFO) by having a clear understanding of the pricing and scope trade-offs that could be made.

quotes.quote: C/CAG reserves the right to not convene oral interviews or discussions, and to make an award on the basis of initial proposals. Accordingly, each initial proposal should be submitted on the most favorable terms from a price and a technical viewpoint. C/CAG reserves the right to negotiate and/or include a best and final offer stage to the process.

findings.title: Contract Duration and Schedule
findings.fact: The total contract duration shall be four (4) years, with the e-bike white paper deliverable completed no later than December 31, 2026. The schedule is based on a project kick-off during the week of April 1, 2026, and completion no later than June 30, 2030.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must commit to a long-term engagement (4 years) and ensure it has the capacity to deliver the e-bike white paper within a tight initial timeframe (by end of 2026). This may affect resource allocation and project planning.
findings.action_recommendation: Develop a detailed project schedule that clearly shows how the e-bike white paper will be completed by December 31, 2026, while also planning for the full 4-year contract. Ensure the bidder has sufficient staff and resources to sustain the project over the entire duration.

quotes.quote: The schedule shall be based on an anticipated project kick-off during the week of April 1, 2026, and shall demonstrate completion of all work no later than June 30, 2030. The total contract duration shall be four (4) years; however, the e-bike white paper deliverable shall be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.

findings.title: Key Personnel Change Approval
findings.fact: Any change in key personnel on the project team is subject to prior written approval of C/CAG. Removal of any key personnel identified in the responses to the RFP without prior written consent of C/CAG may be considered a material breach of contract.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that the key personnel proposed in the proposal are committed to the project for its duration. Any changes could lead to contractual disputes or even termination for breach.
findings.action_recommendation: Before submitting the proposal, confirm with all key personnel that they are available and committed for the entire contract period. Develop a contingency plan for unexpected departures, but be aware that any changes require C/CAG approval and could be risky.

quotes.quote: Any change in key personnel on the project team is subject to prior written approval of C/CAG. Removal of any key personnel identified in the responses to the RFP without prior written consent of C/CAG may be considered a material breach of contract.

findings.title: Evaluation Criteria - Cost Effectiveness
findings.fact: Cost Effectiveness is an evaluation criterion with a weight of 15 points, assessing cost control, budgeting methodology, clarity of cost in spreadsheet format, reasonableness of hourly rates, and allocation of resources.
findings.business_implication: The bidder's cost proposal will be scrutinized for realism and clarity. Unreasonable rates or poor cost control could result in a lower score, affecting the overall competitiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Prepare a detailed cost proposal using the provided template, ensuring all costs are clearly justified and aligned with the scope. Demonstrate a robust budgeting methodology and provide evidence of successful budget management on similar projects.

quotes.quote:
5. Cost Effectiveness (15 points) 
• Cost Control and Budgeting Methodology 
o Proposer has a system or process for managing cost and budget. 
o Evidence of successful budget management for a similar project. 
• Proposal clearly defines cost in spreadsheet format. 
• Reasonableness of hourly rates.  
• Allocation of resources for tasks and activities.

findings.title: Indemnification for Public Records Act Release
findings.fact: By submitting materials, the proposer consents to release of such materials by C/CAG if requested under the Public Records Act without further notice, and agrees to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must be aware that all submitted materials are subject to public disclosure, and the bidder waives any confidentiality claims. Additionally, the bidder must indemnify C/CAG for any release, which could expose the bidder to liability if confidential information is released.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully review all materials for confidential or proprietary information before submission. Consider marking sensitive information, but be aware that the RFP states that all information is a public record. Ensure that the bidder is comfortable with the indemnification obligation and has appropriate insurance coverage.

quotes.quote: By submitting materials, (1) you consent to release of such materials by C/CAG if requested under the Public Records Act without further notice to you, and (2) you agree to indemnify and hold harmless C/CAG for release of such information.

findings.title: Compliance with All Laws
findings.fact: The work performed pursuant to any resulting contract shall comply with the requirements of all federal, state, and local laws without limitation, and shall apply to this RFP and are incorporated into this RFP and any subsequent contract by this reference.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure full compliance with all applicable laws, which may increase operational costs and require specialized legal review. Non-compliance could lead to legal penalties, contract termination, and reputational damage.
findings.action_recommendation: Conduct a thorough legal review of all applicable federal, state, and local laws relevant to the project scope. Develop a compliance plan and allocate resources for ongoing legal monitoring and training.

quotes.quote: The work performed pursuant to any resulting contract shall comply with the requirements of all federal, state, and local laws without limitation, and shall apply to this RFP and are incorporated into this RFP and any subsequent contract by this reference.

findings.title: No Obligation for Proposal Costs
findings.fact: This RFP does not commit C/CAG to award a contract or to pay any costs incurred in the preparation of a proposal in response to this RFP.
findings.business_implication: The bidder bears all costs associated with preparing the proposal, with no guarantee of contract award. This represents a financial risk, especially if the proposal process is lengthy or requires significant resources.
findings.action_recommendation: Carefully evaluate the potential return on investment before committing resources to the proposal. Ensure that the proposal development budget is controlled and that the opportunity aligns with strategic goals.

quotes.quote: This RFP does not commit C/CAG to award a contract or to pay any costs incurred in the preparation of a proposal in response to this RFP.

findings.title: Contract Not Effective Until Fully Executed
findings.fact: Should this RFP result in recommendation for award of a contract, the contract will not have any force or effect until it is approved and fully executed by C/CAG.
findings.business_implication: The bidder cannot begin work or incur costs under the contract until it is fully executed by C/CAG. This creates a period of uncertainty and potential delay between award and contract effectiveness.
findings.action_recommendation: Plan for a potential gap between award notification and contract execution. Avoid incurring any non-recoverable costs until the contract is fully executed. Maintain communication with C/CAG to expedite the execution process.

quotes.quote: Should this RFP result in recommendation for award of a contract, the contract will not have any force or effect until it is approved and fully executed by C/CAG.

findings.title: Termination for Conflict of Interest
findings.fact: C/CAG may terminate the contract if a conflict of interest is discovered and not mitigated, and failure to notify may be grounds for termination for cause.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must proactively identify and disclose any potential conflicts of interest. Failure to do so could result in contract termination and potential legal consequences, damaging the bidder's reputation and relationship with C/CAG.
findings.action_recommendation: Implement a robust conflict of interest policy and conduct thorough checks for all team members and subcontractors. Immediately disclose any potential conflicts to C/CAG and propose mitigation measures. Ensure all staff are trained on these requirements.

quotes.quote: The C/CAG Project Manager may terminate the contract involving the conflict of interest and C/CAG may obtain the conflicted services in any way allowed by law. Failure by the consultant to notify C/CAG Project Manager may be grounds for termination of the contract for cause pursuant to Section 4, Termination, of the Contract Agreement Template, provided as Appendix D to this RFP.

findings.title: Termination for Material Breach Due to Key Personnel Change
findings.fact: Removal of key personnel without prior written consent may be considered a material breach of contract, which could lead to termination.
findings.business_implication: The bidder must ensure that key personnel identified in the proposal remain committed to the project. Any changes could be deemed a material breach, leading to termination and potential liability.
findings.action_recommendation: Secure commitments from key personnel to remain on the project for its duration. If a change is unavoidable, seek prior written consent from C/CAG and provide a suitable replacement with equivalent qualifications. Maintain clear communication with C/CAG regarding any personnel changes.

quotes.quote: Removal of any key personnel identified in the responses to the RFP without prior written consent of C/CAG may be considered a material breach of contract.

findings.title: Contract Term Duration Contradiction
findings.fact: The RFP states the anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months, but also states the total contract duration shall be four (4) years, and the work is expected to commence on April 1, 2026 and be completed no later than June 2030, which is more than 4 years.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity in contract duration may lead to disputes over the actual term and could affect resource planning and pricing. If the contract is interpreted as 48 months, the completion date of June 2030 (which is over 4 years from April 2026) would be inconsistent, potentially causing schedule and cost overruns.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification from C/CAG on the exact contract term and completion date before submitting a proposal. Adjust your work plan and pricing to accommodate the longer timeline if necessary, and ensure your proposal clearly states your understanding of the term.

quotes.quote: The anticipated contract term will be approximately 48 months.
C/CAG expects the work to commence on April 1, 2026 and to be completed no later than June 2030.
The total contract duration shall be four (4) years; however, the e-bike white paper deliverable shall be completed and submitted for final approval no later than December 31, 2026.

findings.title: Project Kick-off Date Contradiction
findings.fact: The tentative schedule lists Notice to Proceed and Project Kick-off on Monday, March 16, 2026, but the Schedule of Work section states the schedule shall be based on an anticipated project kick-off during the week of April 1, 2026.
findings.business_implication: The conflicting kick-off dates create uncertainty about when the project will actually start, which can impact staffing availability, resource allocation, and the ability to meet deadlines. Bidders may need to prepare for an earlier start than expected.
findings.action_recommendation: Clarify the exact kick-off date with C/CAG. In your proposal, indicate your availability to start on either date and provide a flexible schedule that can accommodate both possibilities.

quotes.quote: Monday, March 16, 2026 Notice to Proceed and Project Kick-off
The schedule shall be based on an anticipated project kick-off during the week of April 1, 2026

findings.title: Proposal Page Limit Ambiguity
findings.fact: The RFP states that each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references. However, it also requires an executive summary and project approach (no more than two pages), work plan, schedule of work, and cost proposal, which may cause ambiguity about what counts toward the page limit.
findings.business_implication: The ambiguity in page count could lead to unintentional non-compliance, risking rejection of the proposal. Bidders may inadvertently exceed the limit or omit required content to stay within it, affecting the quality and completeness of the submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Seek clarification on which sections count toward the 20-page limit. Plan your proposal carefully to include all required sections while staying within the limit, and consider using appendices for non-counted items.

quotes.quote: Each submittal shall be no more than 20 pages, excluding cover letter, title page, table of contents, resumes of key staff members, relevant experience, and references.
Provide a brief summary (no more than two pages) of the qualifications and benefits of selecting the proposer to perform requested services.

findings.title: Submittal Requirements Duplicate Section Label
findings.fact: In the Additional Proposal Requirements section, there are two items labeled 'b)': one for Levine Act Disclosure and one for Litigation. This is a formatting error that could cause confusion.
findings.business_implication: The duplicate labeling may cause confusion about the required order and completeness of the additional proposal requirements. Bidders might overlook one of the items or misinterpret the structure, leading to an incomplete submission.
findings.action_recommendation: Ensure both the Levine Act Disclosure and Litigation statements are included in your proposal, regardless of the labeling error. Follow the content requirements and clearly label them to avoid confusion.

b) Litigation
